answer: An agent network curbs Sybil attacks via ambient seismic interferometry across an island. Nodes record microtremors and cross-correlate waveforms against a benchmark seismometer in a subterranean vault. Because elastic wave scattering through a sand dune cannot be simulated in real time, an attacker must deploy discrete geophone hardware per identity. However, storm-induced ocean swells can degrade signal coherence, occasionally triggering false rejections.
